summary: A Blended Program is a parent container of cohort-based Program Batches that mixes self-paced digital learning with instructor-led live and offline sessions: each batch has its own dates, enrolment quota, coordinators and instructors, an approval workflow with bulk CSV approval, session resources, assignments with evaluation, and batch-wise consumption reports.

title: Course
summary: A general platform course is the standard open-access course on iGOT: creators author it in the CBP portal (or generate it with AI), it passes the Course Quality Framework and review before SPV publishing, and every learner can find it, self-enrol into an auto-managed open batch, learn with interactive video, earn a certificate, and unenrol or re-enrol with progress kept.

title: Multilingual
summary: Multilingual courses let one course be offered in several languages: creators add language variants to a live base course in the CBP portal, each variant is reviewed and published on its own, and learners pick a language at enrolment, switch languages while learning, and earn certificates and give ratings per language.

title: Moderated Course
summary: A Moderated Course is a restricted course visible and accessible only to the MDOs it targets, optionally only to Verified Karmayogi profiles: creators set accessSetting and secureSettings in the CBP portal, search hides the course from everyone else, and enrolment, consumption and unenrolment are gated by the same rules.

title: Invite-Only Course / Batch
summary: Invite-only courses, batches and standalone assessments are open only to nominated learners: creators mark content Invite-Only in the CBP portal, auto-batch creation is suppressed, program coordinators create batches and upload the cohort's participant list, and only whitelisted learners can see, enrol in or start the content.

title: Invite-Only Program
summary: An Invite-Only Program is a "Custom users" program container of child courses that only nominated civil servants can find and consume: creators publish it without CQS review, program coordinators run it through mandatory closed batches with bulk CSV invitations, search and direct links are masked for everyone else, and progress rolls up from child courses to a program certificate.

links.label: SRS - Karma Programs and Learner Homepage enhancements

title: Moderated Program
summary: A Moderated Program is an "MDO Specific" program restricted to the ministries, departments and organisations it targets, optionally only to Verified Karmayogi profiles: its child courses must share the program's MDOs, coordinators run it through either one open batch or closed batches, search and direct links are gated for everyone else, and enrolment cascades to the child courses.

title: Moderated Assessment
summary: A Moderated Assessment is a controlled, competency-aligned test for government officials: authors build sectioned question banks that a reviewer approves before publishing, the assessment can be gated behind the prerequisite courses of a curated program, and learners take it in a single timed sitting with server-side scoring, negative marking and certificate issuance on passing.

title: Invite-Only Assessment
summary: An Invite-Only Assessment is a "Custom Users" assessment that only nominated learners can see and attempt: publishing it suppresses the automatic open batch, program coordinators schedule a batch window and invite learners individually or by CSV, and invited learners take a timed, randomised single sitting that is scored server-side.

title: Curated Program
summary: A Curated Program bundles live courses into one Level-2 learning path: creators assemble it in the Content Portal, it passes review and SPV publishing with an auto-created open batch, and learners enrol once, progress through the child courses and, where configured, unlock a gated final program assessment before program certification.

title: Standalone Assessment
summary: An assessment published as its own learning object, outside any course: creators build multi-section question sets with marks-based or psychometric scoring, negative marking, sectional cutoffs and 3x randomization; it is offered openly, MDO-moderated or invite-only in scheduled batches, with resilient test delivery, capped re-attempts and a certificate only on passing.

title: Comprehensive Assessment Program
summary: Comprehensive Assessment (CA) is the program-level assessment tied to an officer's APAR: MDO/CCA admins target reusable user groups with an APAR training plan and a linked CA, learners complete the mandatory courses and attempt the CA (50% pass mark, bounded retakes, never-decrease best score), and the results flow nightly to SPARROW / e-HRMS.

summary: Learning Pathways turns standalone courses into milestone-based curricula: an SPV publisher builds a pathway of up to five milestones with a pre-assessment, mandatory and optional courses and a milestone assessment; learners unlock milestones in sequence, earn achievements per milestone and a completion certificate, and since Q13 skill badges. title: Bharat Kalp
summary: Bharat KALP (Knowledge, Action & Leadership Program) is a restricted microsite for IAS officers in the CBC's leadership programme: a 16-week structured curriculum with progress tracking, curated course recommendations, configurable banners and announcements, private mentorship communities, and program-only talks and podcasts with live meeting links, built by reusing existing platform services.

title: Peer Validation
summary: Peer Validation checks whether learning shows up on the job: SPV and MDO admins link peer validation surveys to published courses; after a configurable delay following completion, the learner is prompted to submit a workplace-application reflection with evidence and nominate validators, who review it and approve or reject it, with submission tracking and reporting for admins.

title: CHS
summary: Content Health Score (CHS) gives every eligible course a 0–100 quality score: a static content-quality score computed within five working days of publication, plus a dynamic learner-performance score from completion, time spent, drop-off, ratings and feedback sentiment, recalculated monthly. Courses are banded Green, Amber or Red so authors, admins and learners can see and act on quality.

title: AI CBP Tool
summary: Turns a department's own Work Allocation Order and other source documents into a designation-by-designation Capacity Building Plan — role profile, competencies, and a course list — reviewed, approved and published by an MDO admin.

title: Search
summary: Platform-wide search: an Elasticsearch-backed content/people/community search fronted by every portal and the mobile app, plus an independent LLM keyword-extraction step that two of five clients call before they search.

title: Events Hub
summary: The synchronous and interactive virtual learning subsystem of the iGOT Karmayogi platform. It governs the full lifecycle of virtual sessions — MDO authoring, SPV editorial review and publishing, cohort-based access control, live streaming and in-session chat, watch-time completion tracking, verifiable certificates, and post-event reporting — linking attendance to the Karmayogi Competency Model.

title: Unenrollment of Courses
summary: Self-unenrollment lets a learner withdraw from an enrolled, not-yet-completed course from the TOC or course-card menu: the enrolment is deactivated, hours, karma and badges are reversed, progress is kept, and the course moves to an Unenrolled tab from which the learner can re-enroll and pick up where they left off.

title: Moderated Content
summary: Two unrelated systems sharing one name: an MDO-restricted courseCategory/secureSettings visibility scheme for Moderated Course/Program/Assessment riding on the generic Sunbird review workflow, and an independent ML text-profanity check on discussion posts.

title: User Onboarding
summary: How a person gets an account — public sign-up, a department's registration link or QR code, an admin adding them, or government single sign-on — and the admin steps behind it. Registering submits a request; the account is created afterwards.

title: SPV & Admin Registration
summary: The platform-owner side of onboarding, done from the SPV / super-admin portal: creating organisations, putting their first administrators in place, publishing registration links, and approving requests for new organisations, designations and email domains.

title: Marketplace
summary: The iGOT Karmayogi Marketplace brings external education partners' courses to civil servants: partners self-register and are approved, their catalogs are ingested, SPVs curate courses as paid or free with seat licences, and learners pass Karma-point gating, launch partner courses over SAML SSO or LTI 1.3, and redeem Karma Coins for paid courses.

title: AI Assessment Tool
summary: AssessAI (the iGOT AI Assessment Generator) generates, evaluates, refines and governs curriculum-aligned assessments: it turns course material or Karmayogi Competency Model selections into KCM- and Bloom-aligned question banks that creators review, edit and export for the LMS.

title: Competency Passbook
summary: The Competency Passbook (Learner Passbook) is a learner's competency record on iGOT: it shows the competencies required for their designation against those already earned through iGOT courses, self-declared external training and ATI/CTI bulk uploads, kept in a real-time Kafka/Flink-fed Cassandra ledger.

title: Discussion Hub
summary: Discuss Hub is the community-scoped discussion engine of iGOT Karmayogi: MDO leaders create competency-mapped Communities under SPV-approved Topics, and members post questions, comments and replies in a 3-level thread, with upvotes, cross-community bookmarks and threshold-based moderation.

title: Bulk Registration
summary: Uploading a CSV of new users to create many accounts at once — except the platform actually has three independent, largely disconnected implementations of this, and the backend endpoint named for "bulk create" creates exactly one user per call.

title: Weekly Claps
summary: Weekly Claps is the learner engagement streak on the home page: a learner earns a clap for every week with at least 60 minutes of platform time, consecutive weeks build a streak that resets after a missed week, and a nightly batch job computes it from telemetry, keeps a rolling four-week history and triggers in-app review prompts for engaged learners.

title: Karma Wallet
summary: The Karma ecosystem rewards learning and lets learners spend it: Karma Points are a permanent, ever-increasing record earned for milestones such as first login, enrolment, course completion, assessments, ratings, live events and ACBP compliance; learners convert them 1:1 into Karma Coins (up to 300 a month) in the Karma Wallet and redeem the coins for marketplace courses, with an append-only transaction history.
